strings.name: Amitabh Bachchan
strings.role: Actor and television host · Hindi cinema
strings.summary: Amitabh Bachchan’s resonant voice and forceful screen presence helped shape a young man confronting injustice in films such as Zanjeer and Deewaar. He also worked in comedy, family drama and action. After a brief political career and professional and financial setbacks, Kaun Banega Crorepati and new film roles renewed his appeal across generations. Later works including Black, Paa and Piku show different directions in his acting.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to television recording news in November 2026. National Film Awards use their announcement or presentation years and identify the relevant films’ years.
strings.influence.rationale: Influenced Indian popular culture through screen roles and television hosting familiar to several generations, becoming a leading figure in Hindi cinema.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Family background
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Son of Hindi poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Shaping a distinctive screen figure
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: In Zanjeer, Deewaar and Sholay, his speech, physicality and emotional intensity influenced acting in popular Hindi cinema.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: A sustained career across film and television
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: From hosting Kaun Banega Crorepati in 2000 onward, continued reaching different generations through television and films such as Piku.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Continues recording KBC’s eighteenth season
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Returned to recording Kaun Banega Crorepati after a short break, continuing more than two decades of television hosting.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Appears in Kalki 2898 AD
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Played Ashwatthama in a film combining mythology with a futuristic setting, continuing his later-career work in genre cinema.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the Dadasaheb Phalke Award
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The President of India presented the national cinema lifetime-achievement honor at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Wins a National Film Award for Piku
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Won Best Actor at the 63rd National Film Awards for his father role in the 2015 film, continuing recognition of his later work.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Stars in Paa
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Played a child with progeria, using makeup, voice and physical performance to transform age and family relationships.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Appears in Black
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Played a teacher in Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s film, expanding his work beyond the action-hero roles of earlier decades.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Begins hosting Kaun Banega Crorepati
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Turned to a television quiz show after professional and financial difficulties, reaching a wide audience through a measured hosting style.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Elected to the Indian Parliament
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Temporarily shifted toward public affairs, entering the Lok Sabha for Allahabad before leaving politics a few years later.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Stars in Deewaar and Sholay
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Strengthened his place in 1970s Hindi cinema through contrasting roles in a crime melodrama and an ensemble action film.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Breaks through with Zanjeer
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Played a policeman confronting injustice, helping establish the intense screen figure later called the “angry young man.”
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Appears in his first film Saat Hindustani
strings.timeline.event-11.text: After leaving work in Calcutta for Bombay, gained an early screen role in an ensemble film, beginning a long acting career.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Allahabad
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born into the family of poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan, growing up in a literary environment before turning to cinema.
